# Summary of Cairn Rules

## Basic Pulse Mechanics
A pulse boosts a cairn's height based on two components: the stride value itself, plus a bonus equal to the number of complete strides contained in the current height. For example, a cairn at height 20 with stride 6 has 3 complete strides within it, so the pulse adds 6 + 3 = 9 marks total.

## Multiple Pulses
When applying several pulses in sequence, each one must be recalculated using the new height from the previous pulse. The height grows, which means each successive pulse typically adds more marks than the last one, creating an accelerating pattern. You cannot simply multiply a single pulse's effect.

## Leaks
A leak is a percentage-based drain tied to the new height after a pulse. It removes one mark for every d marks of height (where d is the leak size). Leaks are applied after the pulse and reduce the final height. Unlike the pulse calculation, leaks depend only on the resulting height, not on how much was added.

## Draining Cycles
A drain is a fixed amount removed each cycle (after every pulse). Unlike leaks, the drain stays constant regardless of height. A cairn survives longer than simple division suggests because each pulse adds height before the drain takes effect.

## Origins (Working Backwards)
Finding a starting height requires testing candidates by applying forward pulses. The ending height uniquely determines the origin because pulses always raise height in predictable ways.

## Merging
Two cairns combine using weighted shares (in tenths) plus a tether offset. Each share is floored to whole numbers before adding, then the tether adjusts the result.
